meaning: Identical source-derived finite Workflow cases with compact expected semantic commitments, preserving the predecessor's semantic inputs, search order, recipe identities and dimensions.
selection: Private Workflow cross-generator protocol only; old Workflow case API, definition, generated code and public defaults remain unchanged. The family holds up to four bounded batches (32 MiB total, 8 MiB per native batch). The new private family ceiling is explicitly 16384 cases; each native batch retains the predecessor 4096-case ceiling. No old profile limit changes.
expected_encoding: SHA-256 of canonical JSON of the complete existing independent Workflow execution observation. This includes outcome, recovery identities, batches, port/read/clock traces, await observations and mutation/getter checks. No field is omitted. Native observations must compute the same commitment from their complete actual observation.

limits.unavailable: Whole family not_evaluable; no truncated or selected prefix.
limits.batching: Every family case must be observed exactly once, in source order across at most four batches. One original-module instance and identity registry span all batches. Missing batches are incomplete, never a passing prefix.

validation: For predecessor families within capacity, all recipes, data, dimensions and search metadata must be byte-equivalent and each new expectation must equal the canonical predecessor observation hash. The complete nested Entity/Value Object/sum/Event family must remain executable as a family.
claim_ceiling: Compact finite commitments rely on SHA-256 collision resistance. They are not exhaustive proof, native execution evidence, retained custody or public integration.
